paras.t: Diaconi sint unius uxoris viri, id est, ultra unam uxorem non habeant, propter sacramentum. Sunt enim quasi vicarii Sponsi cœlestis, cujus Sponsa, puta Ecclesia, una est. Tempore autem Apostoli licuit episcopis, presbyteris, atque diaconis unam habere mulierem: qua defuncta, ad castitatem tenebantur. Nunc vero ex ordinatione summi Pontificis ad perpetuam castitatem tenentur. Qui diaconi filiis suis bene præsint et suis domibus, id est familiis, tam in spiritualibus, quam in temporalibus.
paras.en: [[3:12|Let deacons be the husbands of one wife|Diaconi sint unius uxoris viri]], that is, let them not have more than one wife, on account of the sacrament [that is, the sacred sign: marriage signifies the union of Christ with the Church]. For they are as it were vicars of the heavenly Bridegroom, whose Bride, namely the Church, is one. In the time of the Apostle bishops, priests and deacons were permitted to have one wife; when she died, they were bound to chastity. But now, by ordinance of the supreme Pontiff, they are bound to perpetual chastity. [[3:12|who|Qui]], that is, the deacons, [[3:12|rule well their children and their own houses|filiis suis bene præsint et suis domibus]], that is, their households, in spiritual things as well as in temporal.

paras.t: Qui enim bene ministraverint in minoribus officiis atque ordinibus, gradum sibi bonum acquirent, id est, ad altiorem statum et ordinem promovebuntur, ad propriam et aliorum salutem, et multam fiduciam, id est spem magnam de futura beatitudine: fiduciam, inquam, in fide fundatam, quæ fides est in Christo Jesu sicut in datore, confirmatore et præmiatore.
paras.en: [[3:13|For they that have ministered well|Qui enim bene ministraverint]] in the lesser offices and orders [[3:13|shall purchase to themselves a good degree|gradum sibi bonum acquirent]], that is, they shall be promoted to a higher state and order, for their own salvation and that of others, [[3:13|and much confidence|et multam fiduciam]], that is, great hope of the beatitude to come: a confidence, I say, founded [[3:13|in the faith|in fide]], [[3:13|which is in Christ Jesus|quæ fides est in Christo Jesu]] as in its giver, confirmer and rewarder.

paras.t: Hæc tibi scribo, sperans me venire ad te cito a Laodicia ad Ephesum. Si autem tardavero, tunc scribo ut scias interim ex doctrina hujus epistolæ, quomodo oporteat te in domo Dei, id est in grege fidelium tibi commisso, conversari, omnibus et singulis salubriter præsidendo, exemplariter te habendo, et unicuique proportionatam doctrinam imprimendo. Quæ domus est Ecclesia Dei vivi, id est congregatio Christianorum: Ecclesia utique, non ex vilibus saxis, sed vivis constructa lapidibus; estque columna et firmamentum veritatis, id est, veritatem evangelicam fortiter portat, infirmosque sustinet, et vacillantes confirmat, tanquam firmamentum seu fulcimentum nutantium in fide aut moribus.
paras.en: [[3:14|These things I write to thee, hoping that I shall come to thee shortly|Hæc tibi scribo, sperans me venire ad te cito]], from Laodicia to Ephesus. [[3:15|But if I tarry long|Si autem tardavero]], then I write [[3:15|that thou mayest know|ut scias]] meanwhile, from the teaching of this epistle, [[3:15|how thou oughtest|quomodo oporteat te]] [[3:15|in the house of God|in domo Dei]], that is, in the flock of the faithful committed to thee, [[3:15|to behave thyself|conversari]], presiding over each and all for their salvation, conducting thyself as an example, and impressing on each the teaching suited to him. [[3:15|which|Quæ]] house [[3:15|is the church of the living God|est Ecclesia Dei vivi]], that is, the congregation of Christians: a Church built indeed not of common stones but of living ones[[1 Pet 2:5||]]; and it is [[3:15|the pillar and ground of the truth|columna et firmamentum veritatis]], that is, it bears the gospel truth strongly, sustains the weak and strengthens the wavering, as the ground or prop [*firmamentum seu fulcimentum*: "ground" here is literally a support] of those who totter in faith or in morals.

paras.t: Et manifeste magnum est in Ecclesia pietatis sacramentum, id est Verbum Dei incarnatum in cordibus fidelium habitans: quod dicitur sacramentum, id est sacrum secretum seu res occulta, quia secundum divinam naturam, inaccessibilem habitat lucem. De quo Isaias: Vere, inquit, tu es Deus absconditus. Dicitur etiam sacramentum pietatis, tanquam origo et fons totius misericordiæ, sanctæ Religionis et cultus divini.
paras.en: [[3:16|And evidently great is|Et manifeste magnum est]] in the Church [[3:16|the mystery of godliness|pietatis sacramentum]], that is, the Word of God incarnate, dwelling in the hearts of the faithful: which is called a mystery [*sacramentum*], that is, a sacred secret or hidden thing, because according to his divine nature he [[1 Tim 6:16|inhabiteth light inaccessible|inaccessibilem habitat lucem]]. Of whom Isaias: [[Is 45:15|Verily|Vere]], he says, [[Is 45:15|thou art a hidden God|tu es Deus absconditus]]. It is also called the mystery *of godliness* as the origin and fount of all mercy, of holy religion and of divine worship [*pietas*, "godliness", also means mercy and dutiful devotion].

paras.t: Quod sacramentum manifestatum est, id est, visibiliter apparuit hominibus, in carne assumpta. Verbum enim caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis. Unde apud Isaiam testatur: Sciet populus meus nomen meum in die illa, quia ego ipse qui loquebar, ecce adsum; et iterum, Simul laudabunt, quia oculo ad oculum videbunt, quum convertit Dominus Sion. Justificatum est, id est justum ostensum quantum ad deitatem, vel justum effectum secundum humanitatem, in Spiritu, id est per operationem Spiritus Sancti, testimonium perhibentis de Christo, et animam ejus omni sanctitate implentis. Apparuit angelis, præsertim in ascensione, quando dixerunt: Quis est iste Rex gloriæ? et, Quis est iste qui venit de Edom? Prædicatum est per Apostolos gentibus universis. In omnem enim terram exivit sonus eorum. Unde Propheta: Paravit, inquit, Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium. Creditum est in mundo, id est, homines per fidem receperunt hoc sacramentum, credendo in Christum, juxta illud in Psalmo: Viderunt omnes termini terræ salutare Dei nostri. Assumptum est in gloria, id est, in ascensione ad Patris dextram elevatum atque locatum est, prout apud Marcum legitur: Dominus Jesus assumptus est in cœlum, et sedet a dextris Dei.
paras.en: [[3:16|which|Quod]] mystery [[3:16|was manifested|manifestatum est]], that is, appeared visibly to men, [[3:16|in the flesh|in carne]] that he assumed. For [[John 1:14|the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us|Verbum enim caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis]]. Hence he testifies in Isaias: [[Is 52:6|my people shall know my name in that day: for I myself that spoke, behold I am here|Sciet populus meus nomen meum in die illa, quia ego ipse qui loquebar, ecce adsum]] [the margin gives Is. liii, 6; the words are Is 52:6]; and again: [[Is 52:8|they shall praise together: for they shall see eye to eye when the Lord shall convert Sion|Simul laudabunt, quia oculo ad oculum videbunt, quum convertit Dominus Sion]]. [[3:16|was justified|Justificatum est]], that is, shown to be just as to the Godhead, or made just according to the manhood, [[3:16|in the spirit|in Spiritu]], that is, by the operation of the Holy Spirit, who bore witness of Christ and filled his soul with all holiness. [[3:16|appeared unto angels|Apparuit angelis]], above all at the ascension, when they said: [[Ps 23:8|Who is this King of Glory?|Quis est iste Rex gloriæ?]] [the margin gives Ps. xxiii, 8 and 10; the question stands in both verses] and, [[Is 63:1|Who is this that cometh from Edom|Quis est iste qui venit de Edom]]? [[3:16|hath been preached|Prædicatum est]] by the Apostles [[3:16|unto the Gentiles|gentibus universis]], all of them. For [[Ps 18:5|Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|In omnem enim terram exivit sonus eorum]]. Hence the Prophet: [[Is 52:10|The Lord hath prepared his holy arm in the sight of all the Gentiles|Paravit, inquit, Dominus brachium sanctum suum in oculis omnium gentium]]. [[3:16|is believed in the world|Creditum est in mundo]], that is, men received this mystery by faith, believing in Christ, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 97:3|All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God|Viderunt omnes termini terræ salutare Dei nostri]]. [[3:16|is taken up in glory|Assumptum est in gloria]], that is, at the ascension it was raised up and set at the right hand of the Father, as we read in Mark: [[Mark 16:19|the Lord Jesus|Dominus Jesus]] [[Mark 16:19|was taken up into heaven and sitteth on the right hand of God|assumptus est in cœlum, et sedet a dextris Dei]].

4.title: DECLARATIO CAPITULI QUARTI : SPIRITUS AUTEM MANIFESTE DICIT, ETC.
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: Now the Spirit manifestly saith, etc.

paras.t: Quoniam jacula prævisa minus feriunt, prænuntiat Apostolus mala Ecclesiæ eventura, ut quum venerint, minus turbentur fideles. Spiritus autem manifeste dicit, id est, Spiritus Sanctus nobis evidenter revelat, quia in novissimis temporibus, maxime circa adventum Antichristi, discedent quidam, etiam famosi et magni, a fide catholica : a qua non corpore, sed corde disceditur, sicut et corde creditur; attendentes spiritibus erroris, id est animabus hominum errantium, seu dæmonibus ad errorem ducentibus, qui in veritate non steterunt, et doctrinis dæmoniorum, quas dæmones per se ingerunt cordibus perversorum, vel per hæreticos proponunt eas simplicibus, in hypocrisi, id est in simulata sanctitate, loquentium mendacium. Dæmonia enim, id est homines dæmone informati, loquuntur falsa cum simulata sanctitate, ut sibi credatur. De quibus dicit in Evangelio Christus : Attendite a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces.
paras.en: Since darts foreseen strike less hard, the Apostle foretells the evils that are to befall the Church, so that when they come the faithful may be less troubled. [[4:1|Now the Spirit manifestly saith|Spiritus autem manifeste dicit]], that is, the Holy Ghost plainly reveals to us, [[4:1|that in the last times|quia in novissimis temporibus]], above all about the coming of Antichrist, [[4:1|some shall depart|discedent quidam]], even famous and great men, [[4:1|from the faith|a fide]], the Catholic faith, from which one departs not with the body but with the heart, just as it is also with the heart that one believes; [[4:1|giving heed to spirits of error|attendentes spiritibus erroris]], that is, to the souls of men in error, or to demons who lead into error, who stood not in the truth, [[4:1|and doctrines of devils|et doctrinis dæmoniorum]], which the demons thrust by themselves into the hearts of the perverse, or set before the simple through heretics; [[4:2|Speaking lies|loquentium mendacium]] [[4:2|in hypocrisy|in hypocrisi]], that is, in feigned holiness. For the devils, that is, men shaped by the devil, speak falsehoods with feigned holiness, so that they may be believed. Of them Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 7:15|Beware of false prophets, who come to you in the clothing of sheep, but inwardly they are ravening wolves|Attendite a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces]].

paras.t: Cauteriatam, id est læsam seu vitiose corruptam, habentium suam conscientiam ; prohibentium nubere, quasi matrimonium non esset sacramentum atque divinitus institutum; jubentium etiam abstinere a cibis quos Deus creavit, quoad primordialem materiam, ad percipiendum eos, id est ad vescendum, cum gratiarum actione : creavit, inquam, eos fidelibus et his qui cognoverunt veritatem, id est ad sustentationem credentium.
paras.en: [[4:2|and having their conscience|habentium suam conscientiam]] [[4:2|seared|Cauteriatam]], that is, injured or viciously corrupted; [[4:3|Forbidding to marry|prohibentium nubere]], as though matrimony were not a sacrament and instituted by God; and bidding them [[4:3|to abstain from meats, which God hath created|abstinere a cibis quos Deus creavit]], as to their first matter, [[4:3|to be received|ad percipiendum eos]], that is, to be eaten, [[4:3|with thanksgiving|cum gratiarum actione]]: He created them, I say, [[4:3|by the faithful and by them that have known the truth|fidelibus et his qui cognoverunt veritatem]], that is, for the sustenance of believers [Denis takes the dative *fidelibus* as 'for the faithful', where the Douay-Rheims has 'by the faithful'].

paras.t: […] est tanquam in sua natura nocivus, qui comedi potest aut solet cum gratiarum actione. Nam licet fideles a certis cibis et potibus interim abstineant, hoc tamen non faciunt ea ratione qua fiebat in veteri Testamento, sed ob corporis castigationem.
paras.en: […] [the start of the gloss on verse 4 is lost in the transcription] is, as it were, harmful in its own nature, if it can be or is wont to be eaten [[4:4|with thanksgiving|cum gratiarum actione]]. For although the faithful at times abstain from certain foods and drinks, they do not do so for the reason for which it was done in the Old Testament, but for the chastisement of the body.

paras.t: Sanctificatur enim per Verbum Dei, id est, a Verbo seu Filio Dei cibus benedicitur, ne sit nocivus, sed utilis. Christus quoque seu Verbum Dei, suo adventu cibos in lege prohibitos, fecit licitos, sicque sanctificavit eos. Et orationem, id est per orationem hominum instrumentaliter, qui sua prece obtinent a Filio Dei sanctificationem ciborum.
paras.en: [[4:5|For it is sanctified by the word of God|Sanctificatur enim per Verbum Dei]] [Denis takes *Verbum Dei* as the Word, the Son of God], that is, food is blessed by the Word or Son of God, so that it may not be harmful but profitable. Christ too, or the Word of God, by His coming made lawful the foods forbidden in the Law, and so sanctified them; [[4:5|and prayer|Et orationem]], that is, through the prayer of men, as instruments, who by their prayer obtain from the Son of God the sanctification of foods.

paras.t: Hæc documenta proponens fratribus per modum exhortationis seu jussionis, bonus eris minister, id est fructuosus prælatus laudabilisque vicarius, Christi Jesu, […] ejus efficaciter instruendo, enutritus, id est spiritualiter educatus ac fotus, verbis fidei et bonæ doctrinæ, id est verbis sacræ Scripturæ, pertinentibus ad fidem sacram evangelicamque doctrinam. Hæc verba animam nutriunt, juxta illud : Non in solo pane vivit homo, sed in omni verbo quod procedit de ore Dei. Quorum doctrinam assecutus, id est adeptus, es […]nationem divinam et meam instructionem.
paras.en: [[4:6|These things proposing to the brethren|Hæc documenta proponens fratribus]] [*hæc documenta*, 'these teachings'] by way of exhortation or command, [[4:6|thou shalt be a good minister|bonus eris minister]], that is, a fruitful prelate and praiseworthy vicar, [[4:6|of Christ Jesus|Christi Jesu]], instructing His […] effectively, [[4:6|nourished up|enutritus]], that is, spiritually brought up and fostered, [[4:6|in the words of faith and of the good doctrine|verbis fidei et bonæ doctrinæ]], that is, in the words of holy Scripture, which belong to the sacred faith and the doctrine of the Gospel. These words nourish the soul, according to that saying: [[Matt 4:4|Not in bread alone doth man live, but in every word that proceedeth from the mouth of God|Non in solo pane vivit homo, sed in omni verbo quod procedit de ore Dei]][[Deut 8:3||]] [the margin gives Deut. viii, 3 and Matth. iv, 4; Denis's wording is that of Matthew]. The doctrine of which [[4:6|thou hast attained unto|assecutus]], that is, obtained, through divine […] and my instruction.

paras.t: Ineptas autem, id est inconvenientes, quibus nec fides nec virtus ædificatur, et aniles fabulas, quales solent recitari a […]. Unde apud Petrum quo[…]tur : Non indoctas fabulas secuti, notam […]m vobis fecimus Domini nostri […] benignitatem cordialem.
paras.en: But [[4:7|foolish|Ineptas]], that is, unfitting, by which neither faith nor virtue is built up, [[4:7|and old wives fables|et aniles fabulas]], such as are wont to be told by […]. Hence in Peter also […]: [[2 Pet 1:16|For we have not by following artificial fables|Non indoctas fabulas secuti]] [Denis reads *indoctas*, 'unlearned', where the Vulgate has *doctas*, 'learned' or 'artful'] [[2 Pet 1:16|made known to you|vobis fecimus]] [[2 Pet 1:16|of our Lord|Domini nostri]] […] [the rest of this passage, with the gloss on the end of verse 7, is lost in the transcription] heartfelt kindness.

paras.t: Nam corporalis exercitatio ad modicum utilis est, id est, exteriora ista exercitia ac instrumenta virtutum, videlicet abstinentiæ, jejunia, vigiliæ, disciplinæ, per se parum proficiunt, nisi in interioribus anima vere virtuosa ac pia reddatur. Unde nonnulli in his corporalibus exercitiis se fatigantes, in caritate et pietate ac interiori perfectione parum proficiunt, quia non ordinant prudenter et indesinenter media ista ad puritatem internam. Pietas autem præfata, ad omnia, id est ad omnem gratiam promerendam, et ad propriam ac aliorum salutem procurandam, utilis est, promissionem, id est promissam mercedem, habens vitæ quæ nunc est, id est vitæ præsentis (nunc enim pietati promittitur sufficientia temporalium, et abundantia spiritualium gratiarum), et futuræ vitæ in patria, in qua merces pietatis est vita seu beatitudo æterna : quemadmodum ait Salvator, Centuplum accipiet, et vitam æternam possidebit.
paras.en: [[4:8|For bodily exercise is profitable to little|Nam corporalis exercitatio ad modicum utilis est]], that is, these outward exercises and instruments of the virtues, namely abstinences, fasts, vigils, disciplines [that is, scourgings undertaken as penance], profit little of themselves, unless the soul is made truly virtuous and godly within. Hence some who weary themselves in these bodily exercises make little progress in charity and godliness and inward perfection, because they do not order these means prudently and unceasingly to inward purity. [[4:8|but godliness|Pietas autem]] [*pietas*: godliness, piety, and also dutiful kindness] spoken of above [[4:8|is profitable to all things|ad omnia]], that is, for meriting all grace and for securing one's own salvation and that of others, [[4:8|having|habens]] [[4:8|promise|promissionem]], that is, the promised reward, [[4:8|of the life that now is|vitæ quæ nunc est]], that is, of the present life (for now there is promised to godliness a sufficiency of temporal things and an abundance of spiritual graces), [[4:8|and of that which is to come|et futuræ]], the life in the fatherland, in which the reward of godliness is everlasting life or beatitude: as the Saviour says, [[Matt 19:29|shall receive an hundredfold, and shall possess life everlasting|Centuplum accipiet, et vitam æternam possidebit]].

paras.t: Fidelis sermo et omni acceptione dignus est, quem de laude pietatis jam intuli. In hoc enim sermone, id est propter hujus sermonis veritatem, laboramus in interioribus et exterioribus exercitiis pietatis, et maledicimur a perversis quasi inique agentes. Sed ideo constanter laboramus et omnia æquanimiter toleramus, quia speramus in Deum vivum, id est, sperando in Deum tendimus, exspectando futuram felicitatem ab eo : quæ tanta est ut non sint condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad eam ; qui est salvator omnium hominum, maxime fidelium. Trinitas quippe supergloriosa est salvator principalis, quæ per Christi mysteria nos redemit. Et sicut Christus vocatur salvator omnium quoad sufficientiam, electorum vero quantum ad efficientiam ; sic Deus Trinitas est salvator omnium per sufficientiam, fidelium vero fide et opere est salvator per efficientiam, quos ad salutem perducit cœlestem.
paras.en: [[4:9|A faithful saying and worthy of all acceptation|Fidelis sermo et omni acceptione dignus est]] is the saying which I have just brought forward in praise of godliness. [[4:10|For therefore|In hoc enim]] [literally 'For in this'] saying, that is, on account of the truth of this saying, [[4:10|we labour|laboramus]] in the inward and outward exercises of godliness, [[4:10|and are reviled|et maledicimur]] by the perverse, as though we did wickedly. But we labour steadfastly and bear all things with an even mind for this reason, [[4:10|because we hope in the living God|quia speramus in Deum vivum]], that is, by hoping we tend towards God, looking for the happiness to come from Him, which is so great that [[Rom 8:18|the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared|non sint condignæ passiones hujus temporis]] with it; [[4:10|who is the Saviour of all men, especially of the faithful|qui est salvator omnium hominum, maxime fidelium]]. For the supremely glorious Trinity is the principal Saviour, who redeemed us through the mysteries of Christ. And as Christ is called the Saviour of all as to sufficiency, but of the elect as to efficacy, so God the Trinity is the Saviour of all by sufficiency, but of those faithful in faith and in deed He is the Saviour by efficacy, and brings them to heavenly salvation.

paras.t: Præcipe hæc quæ de fabularum inanium vitatione et pietatis exercitatione tibi jam jussi, subditis tuis, et doce eos, si qui eorum hæc nesciant.
paras.en: [[4:11|These things command|Præcipe hæc]], which I have just bidden thee concerning the avoiding of empty fables and the exercise of godliness, to thy subjects, [[4:11|and teach|et doce]] them, if any of them do not know these things.

paras.t: Consequenter docet prælatum a suis subditis honorandum. Nemo adolescentiam tuam, id est te adolescentem, contemnat, parvi pendendo verba tua ac jussa propter adolescentiam tuam, quasi inexpertus sis et imperfectus. Et ut hoc alii diligenter observent, oportet ut vita et moribus annos tuos excedas, habendo te mature in omnibus. Ideo subditur : sed exemplum esto fidelium in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate, in fide, in castitate, id est, in his omnibus habe te exemplariter et sincere, quatenus loquendo, operando, diligendo, credendo, seu opera caritatis ac fidei ostendendo, et caste vivendo, alios ædifices, et similes tui efficias.
paras.en: Next he teaches that a prelate is to be honoured by his subjects. [[4:12|Let no man|Nemo]] [[4:12|despise|contemnat]] [[4:12|thy youth|adolescentiam tuam]], that is, thee as a young man, making little of thy words and commands because of thy youth, as though thou wert inexperienced and imperfect. And that others may carefully observe this, thou must go beyond thy years in life and manners, bearing thyself maturely in all things. Therefore it is added: [[4:12|but be thou an example of the faithful, in word, in conversation, in charity, in faith, in chastity|sed exemplum esto fidelium in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate, in fide, in castitate]], that is, in all these bear thyself as an example and sincerely, so that by speaking, working, loving, believing, or showing works of charity and faith, and by living chastely, thou mayest edify others and make them like thyself.

paras.t: Dum venio ad te, videlicet interim et tunc, attende lectioni sacræ Scripturæ, in qua Spiritus Sanctus cum homine loquitur, et homo quasi in speculo conspicit quid agere debeat, exhortationi proximorum, et doctrinæ, id est informationi ignorantium : faciendo hos actus successive ac ordinate, videlicet congruo loco et tempore studendo, postmodum exhortando sive docendo.
paras.en: [[4:13|Till I come|Dum venio]] to thee, that is, meanwhile and then, [[4:13|attend unto reading|attende lectioni]] of holy Scripture, in which the Holy Ghost speaks with man, and man sees as in a mirror what he ought to do; [[4:13|to exhortation|exhortationi]] of thy neighbours, [[4:13|and to doctrine|et doctrinæ]], that is, the instruction of the ignorant: doing these acts in succession and in order, namely studying at the fitting place and time, and afterwards exhorting or teaching.

paras.t: Deinde hortatur Timotheum ad diligentem sui officii exsecutionem. Noli negligere, id est per pigritiam perdere vel dissimulare, et ab operibus bonis suspendere, gratiam gratum facientem, seu gratis datam, id est supernaturale donum Spiritus Sancti, seu ordinem episcopatus, quæ data est tibi a Deo per prophetiam, id est propheticam revelationem mihi de te factam, qua mihi ostensum est te viriliter exsecuturum episcopale officium. Quæ etiam gratia data est tibi cum impositione, id est per impositionem, manuum presbyterii, id est manuum mearum, qui te ordinavi episcopum : per quam impositionem, presbyterium seu sacerdotium tibi collatum est cum gratia sacramentali, quæ confertur in sacramentis evangelicæ legis. Vel, ponit abstractum pro concreto, videlicet presbyterium pro presbytero.
paras.en: Then he exhorts Timothy to the diligent carrying out of his office. [[4:14|Neglect not|Noli negligere]], that is, do not lose through sloth, or pass over, and keep back from good works, [[4:14|the grace|gratiam]] that makes pleasing, or that is freely given [that is, *gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes its bearer pleasing to God, or *gratia gratis data*, a gift freely given for the good of others], that is, the supernatural gift of the Holy Ghost, or the order of the episcopate, [[4:14|which was given thee|quæ data est tibi]] by God [[4:14|by prophecy|per prophetiam]], that is, by the prophetic revelation made to me about thee, by which it was shown me that thou wouldst carry out the episcopal office manfully. This grace too was given thee [[4:14|with imposition|cum impositione]], that is, through the imposition, [[4:14|of the hands of the priesthood|manuum presbyterii]], that is, of my hands, who ordained thee bishop: through which imposition the presbyterate or priesthood was conferred on thee together with sacramental grace, which is conferred in the sacraments of the law of the Gospel. Or, he puts the abstract for the concrete, namely *presbyterium* for *presbyter* [that is, 'the priesthood' for 'the priest'].

paras.t: Deinceps admonet Timotheum ad seriosam obedientiam eorum quæ ipse scribit et mandat ei. Hæc quæ tibi præcepi, meditare : quemadmodum apud Sapientem dicitur : Serva mandata et legem quasi pupillam oculi tui : liga eam in digitis tuis, et in tabulis cordis tui scribe eam ; in his esto occupatus per obedientiam, ut profectus tuus in sancta conversatione, manifestus sit omnibus, ad ædificationem eorum et gloriam Dei, non ad tuum præconium.
paras.en: Next he admonishes Timothy to earnest obedience to what he himself writes and commands him. [[4:15|Meditate upon these things|Hæc quæ tibi præcepi, meditare]] which I have commanded thee, as it is said in the Wise Man: [[Prov 7:2|Keep my commandments|Serva mandata]] [[Prov 7:2|and my law as the apple of thy eye|et legem quasi pupillam oculi tui]]: [[Prov 7:3|Bind it upon thy fingers|liga eam in digitis tuis]], and [[Prov 7:3|write it upon the tables of thy heart|in tabulis cordis tui scribe eam]]; [[4:15|be wholly in these things|in his esto]], busied in them through obedience, [[4:15|that thy profiting|ut profectus tuus]] in holy conversation [[4:15|may be manifest to all|manifestus sit omnibus]], for their edification and the glory of God, not for thy own renown.

paras.t: Attende tibi primum, ut vivas sicut decet episcopum, et doctrinæ, id est, consequenter intende instructioni gregis tui. Qui enim sibi ipsi nequam est, cui bonus est? Et, Quid proficit homo si lucretur universum mundum, se ipsum autem perdat? Hoc etiam in Actibus ait Apostolus : Attendite vobis et universo gregi, in quo posuit vos Spiritus Sanctus episcopos. Insta in illis, diligenter vacando tibi et aliis. Hoc enim faciens, et te ipsum salvum facies, id est, beatitudinem promereberis, et eos qui te audiunt, non solum auribus corporis, sed etiam cordis, salvos facies accidenter, cooperative ac instrumentaliter.
paras.en: [[4:16|Take heed to thyself|Attende tibi]] first, so as to live as befits a bishop, [[4:16|and to doctrine|et doctrinæ]], that is, then attend to the instruction of thy flock. For [[Ecclus 14:5|He that is evil to himself, to whom will he be good?|Qui enim sibi ipsi nequam est, cui bonus est?]] And: [[Luke 9:25|what is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world and lose himself|Quid proficit homo si lucretur universum mundum, se ipsum autem perdat?]]? This the Apostle also says in the Acts: [[Acts 20:28|Take heed to yourselves and to the whole flock, wherein the Holy Ghost hath placed you bishops|Attendite vobis et universo gregi, in quo posuit vos Spiritus Sanctus episcopos]]. [[4:16|be earnest in them|Insta in illis]], diligently giving thy time to thyself and to others. [[4:16|For in doing this|Hoc enim faciens]] [[4:16|thou shalt both save thyself|et te ipsum salvum facies]], that is, thou shalt merit beatitude, [[4:16|and them that hear thee|et eos qui te audiunt]], not only with the ears of the body but also with those of the heart, thou shalt save, accidentally, cooperatively and instrumentally [that is, not as the principal cause of their salvation, which is God, but as one working with Him and as His instrument].

5.title: EXPLANATIO CAPITULI QUINTI : SENIOREM NE INCREPAVERIS, SED OBSECRA UT PATREM.
5.title_en: Explanation of the fifth chapter: An ancient man rebuke not, but entreat him as a father.

paras.t: Præterea docet Apostolus modum docendi in speciali, quatenus unusquisque instruatur secundum status sui decentiam. Seniorem ætate et moribus ne increpaveris, arguendo eum duris sermonibus, ne ad indignationem concitetur, et quia non decet: nisi forte ad exercitandum vel ad aliorum ædificationem, sicut frequenter viri sancti sanctissimos seniores dure increpasse leguntur; sed obsecra ut patrem, id est, humiliter ac suppliciter admone eum ut indecentia corrigat in se ipso vel aliis. Tamen, ut ait Gregorius, seniores leves et vitiosos, durissime arguendi sunt. Unde Sapiens ait: Senectus venerabilis est, non diuturna, neque annorum numero computata; sed ætas senectutis, vita immaculata. De tali sene in Levitico legitur: Coram cano capite consurge, et honora personam senis. Juvenes obsecra ad proficiendum in bonis, et abstinendum a malis, ut fratres, ut tua humilitate et caritate mollita atque compuncti, citius acquiescant. Anus, id est vetulas, obsecra hoc modo, ut matres tuas spirituales, vel sicut decet matres rogari a filiis. Juvenculas obsecra ut sorores in omni castitate, ita ut nullo modo habeas te ad eas petulanter, impudice sive carnaliter.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle teaches the manner of teaching in particular, so that each one may be instructed according to what befits his state. [[5:1|An ancient man|Seniorem]], in age and in conduct, [[5:1|rebuke not|ne increpaveris]] by reproving him with harsh words, lest he be stirred to indignation, and because it is not seemly: unless perhaps to exercise him, or for the edification of others, as holy men are often read to have rebuked most holy elders harshly; [[5:1|but entreat him as a father|sed obsecra ut patrem]], that is, admonish him humbly and suppliantly to correct what is unbecoming in himself or in others. Yet, as Gregory says, elders who are light and vicious are to be reproved most severely. Hence the Wise Man says: [[Wis 4:8|venerable old age is not that of long time, nor counted by the number of years|Senectus venerabilis est, non diuturna, neque annorum numero computata]]; but [[Wis 4:9|a spotless life is old age|ætas senectutis, vita immaculata]]. Of such an old man we read in Leviticus: [[Lev 19:32|Rise up before the hoary head, and honour the person of the aged man|Coram cano capite consurge, et honora personam senis]]. [[5:1|young men|Juvenes]] entreat to make progress in good things and to abstain from evil, [[5:1|as brethren|ut fratres]], so that, softened and pricked to the heart by thy humility and charity, they may yield the sooner. [[5:2|Old women|Anus]], that is, aged women, entreat in this way, [[5:2|as mothers|ut matres]], thy spiritual mothers, or as it befits mothers to be asked by their children. [[5:2|young women|Juvenculas]] entreat [[5:2|as sisters, in all chastity|ut sorores in omni castitate]], so that in no way thou bear thyself towards them wantonly, immodestly or carnally.

paras.t: Viduas honora, ministrando eis necessaria vitæ, si pauperes sint, vel reverentiam solam exhibendo, si fuerint divites: quod intelligo de his quæ vere viduæ sunt, id est, vitam suo statui convenientem ducunt, tanquam separatæ a solatio amoreque sæculi, sicut destitutæ sunt a solatio viri. Denique, de divitibus viduis subditur: Si qua autem, id est aliqua, vidua filios aut nepotes habet, ejus educatione et instructione egentes, discat primum, id est, antequam alienis præficiatur, domum suam, id est propriam familiam, bene […], et mutuam vicem reddere parentibus suis, si vivant, quatenus sicut ab eis nutrita est, sic nutriat eos, si fuerit opportunum. […] Deo. Quæ autem vere vidua est, secundum sensum præfatum. Si desolata, id est pauper et sola, non habens familiam, speret in Deum, id est, totam suam fiduciam in Deo constituat, certa quod Ecclesia sibi de necessariis providebit; instet obsecrationibus et orationibus nocte ac die, id est competentibus horis diurnis atque nocturnis, totaliter occupando se in divinis, et orando pro se ipsa ac aliis quorum eleemosynis sustentatur ut sic vacet divinis.
paras.en: [[5:3|Honour widows|Viduas honora]], by ministering to them the necessaries of life if they are poor, or by showing them reverence only if they are rich: which I understand of those [[5:3|that are widows indeed|quæ vere viduæ sunt]], that is, who lead a life befitting their state, as being parted from the comfort and love of the world, just as they are bereft of the comfort of a husband. Then, of rich widows, it is added: [[5:4|But if any|Si qua autem]], that is, some, [[5:4|widow have children or grandchildren|vidua filios aut nepotes habet]] who need bringing up and instruction, [[5:4|let her learn first|discat primum]], that is, before she is set over others, [[5:4|her own house|domum suam]], that is, her own household, well […], [[5:4|and to make a return of duty to her parents|et mutuam vicem reddere parentibus suis]], if they are living, so that as she was nourished by them, so she may nourish them, if need be. […] God. [[5:5|But she that is a widow indeed|Quæ autem vere vidua est]], in the sense given above. If [[5:5|desolate|desolata]], that is, poor and alone, having no household, [[5:5|let her trust in God|speret in Deum]], that is, let her place all her confidence in God, certain that the Church will provide her with what she needs; [[5:5|continue in supplications and prayers night and day|instet obsecrationibus et orationibus nocte ac die]], that is, at the fitting hours of the day and of the night, occupying herself wholly in divine things, and praying for herself and for the others by whose alms she is supported, so that she may thus be free for divine things.

paras.t: Sic ergo agendum est viduæ: Nam quæ in deliciis est, id est carnaliter vivens et mundi delicias quærens, vivens vita naturæ, mortua est, carendo vita gratiæ propter peccatum mortale. De qua morte ait in Evangelio Christus: Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos. Et hoc præcipe viduis, ut irreprehensibiles sint, delicias corporales et magna ac notabilia peccata vitando.
paras.en: This, then, is how a widow must act. [[5:6|For she that liveth in pleasures|Nam quæ in deliciis est]], that is, living carnally and seeking the delights of the world, [[5:6|while she is living|vivens vita]] the life of nature, [[5:6|is dead|mortua est]], lacking the life of grace through mortal sin. Of this death Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 8:22|let the dead bury their dead|Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos]]. [[5:7|And this give in charge|Et hoc præcipe]] to widows, [[5:7|that they may be blameless|ut irreprehensibiles sint]], by shunning bodily pleasures and great and notable sins.

paras.t: Quod autem vidua dives, vel valens, propriam domum regere debeat, patet ex hoc: Si quis autem suorum propinquorum, et maxime domesticorum, ut sunt parentes et filii, curam non habet, eos regendo seu nutriendo; fidem negavit, bona fidei omittendo, quamvis ore non exprimat: sicut de quibusdam testatur Scriptura, Dicunt se nosse Deum, factis autem negant; et est infideli qui nondum veritatem fidei audivit, deterior, saltem quantum ad aliquid, vel ceteris paribus. Agit enim contra Christum, qui in cruce suspensus, de Matre sua sollicitus fuit, commendans eam discipulo. Propter quod etiam Petrus: Melius est, inquit, viam justitiæ non cognoscere, quam post agnitionem converti retrorsum.
paras.en: Now that a widow who is rich, or able, ought to govern her own house is clear from this: [[5:8|But if any man|Si quis autem]] [[5:8|of his own|suorum]] kinsfolk, [[5:8|and especially of those of his house|et maxime domesticorum]], such as parents and children, [[5:8|have not care|curam non habet]] by ruling or nourishing them, [[5:8|he hath denied the faith|fidem negavit]], by leaving undone the good works of faith, though he does not say so with his mouth: as Scripture testifies of certain men, [[Tit 1:16|that they know God: but in their works they deny him|Dicunt se nosse Deum, factis autem negant]] [Denis has *Dicunt*, they say, where the Vulgate has *Confitentur*, they profess]; [[5:8|and is|et est]] [[5:8|worse|deterior]] [[5:8|than an infidel|infideli]], one who has not yet heard the truth of the faith, at least in some respect, or other things being equal. For he acts against Christ, who, hanging on the cross, was solicitous for his Mother, commending her to the disciple[[John 19:26||]][[John 19:27||]]. Wherefore Peter too says: [[2 Pet 2:21|it had been better|Melius est]], he says, [[2 Pet 2:21|not to have known the way of justice than, after they have known it, to turn back|viam justitiæ non cognoscere, quam post agnitionem converti retrorsum]].

paras.t: Consequenter docet quales viduæ sint eleemosynis Ecclesiæ sustentandæ. Vidua eligatur, id est, talis vidua suscipiatur ab Ecclesia sustentanda, non minus sexaginta annorum, id est, quæ ad minus sexagenaria sit. Talis namque caret signo suspicionis, eo quod in tanta ætate exstinctus sit fervor libidinis: idcirco secure nutritur a ministris Ecclesiæ. Quæ fuerit unius viri uxor dumtaxat: quod est signum continentiæ. Debet enim unius tantum viri uxor fuisse, propter sacramentum copulæ Christi et Ecclesiæ, quæ est unius cum una, videlicet Christi cum sponsa sua Ecclesia. In operibus bonis, id est de laudabili sua præterita conversatione, testimonium habens a fide dignis. De quibus operibus subditur: si filios suos educavit in cibis ac moribus, si hospitio recepit peregrinos ac pauperes, si sanctorum pedes lavit, præsertim prædicatorum undique discurrentium: quos in primitiva Ecclesia periculosum erat recipere; si tribulationem patientibus, id est afflictis, captivis, oppressis atque similibus, subministravit, necessaria tribuendo, vel obsequium impendendo, si omne opus bonum ad se pertinens subsecuta est per operationem assiduam.
paras.en: Next he teaches what kind of widows are to be supported by the alms of the Church. [[5:9|Let a widow be chosen|Vidua eligatur]], that is, let such a widow be taken up by the Church to be supported, [[5:9|of no less than threescore years of age|non minus sexaginta annorum]], that is, one who is at least sixty years old. For such a one is free of any mark of suspicion, since at so great an age the heat of lust is quenched: therefore she is safely maintained by the ministers of the Church. [[5:9|who hath been the wife of one husband|Quæ fuerit unius viri uxor]] only: which is a sign of continence. For she must have been the wife of one husband only, on account of the sacrament of the union of Christ and the Church, which is of one with one, namely of Christ with his spouse the Church. [[5:10|Having testimony|testimonium habens]] from persons worthy of belief [[5:10|for her good works|In operibus bonis]], that is, for her praiseworthy past way of life. Of which works it is added: [[5:10|if she have brought up children|si filios suos educavit]], in food and in conduct; [[5:10|if she have received to harbour|si hospitio recepit]] pilgrims and the poor; [[5:10|if she have washed the saints' feet|si sanctorum pedes lavit]], especially those of the preachers who went about everywhere, whom it was dangerous to receive in the early Church; [[5:10|if she have ministered|subministravit]] [[5:10|to them that suffer tribulation|si tribulationem patientibus]], that is, to the afflicted, to captives, to the oppressed and the like, by giving them what they need or by doing them service; [[5:10|if she have diligently followed|subsecuta est]] [[5:10|every good work|si omne opus bonum]] that belongs to her, by constant working.

paras.t: Adolescentiores autem viduas, quæ nondum sexaginta annos sortitæ sunt, devita, id est, non eas suscipias Ecclesiæ elemosynis sustentandas, nec votum continentiæ usque adeo ab eis requiras, propter vitanda pericula. Talium enim sanguis fervet, nec lubricæ ætati facile est credendum. Ideo autem vitandæ sunt: Quum enim luxuriatæ fuerint, luxuriose, gulose seu deliciose vivendo post continentiæ votum, in Christo, id est quasi honeste ac licite, nubere volunt, non arbitrantes hoc esse culpabile, eo quod excæcata sit ratio earum concupiscentiis carnis; habentes damnationem, id est causam damnationis æternæ, videlicet mortale peccatum, quia primam fidem, id est continentiæ promissionem, irritam fecerunt, id est violaverunt. Promittentibus namque castitatem non solum nubere, sed et velle nubere, est damnabile. Simul autem, id est una cum peccatis jam memoratis, et otiosæ existentes discunt circuire domos aliorum, hinc inde vagando; non solum otiosæ, quoniam otiositas non est diu sola, sed parit alia vitia, sed et verbosæ et curiosæ: verbositas enim et curiositas ex otiositate nascuntur; loquentes quæ non oportet, id est illicita et nociva. Minus dicit, et majus significat.
paras.en: [[5:11|But the younger widows|Adolescentiores autem viduas]], who have not yet reached sixty years, [[5:11|avoid|devita]], that is, do not take them up to be supported by the alms of the Church, nor be so ready to require of them a vow of continence, so as to avoid dangers. For the blood of such is hot, and a slippery age is not easily to be trusted. And they are to be avoided for this reason: [[5:11|For when they have grown wanton|Quum enim luxuriatæ fuerint]], by living wantonly, gluttonously or delicately after the vow of continence, [[5:11|in Christ|in Christo]], that is, as if honestly and lawfully, [[5:11|they will marry|nubere volunt]], not thinking this blameworthy, because their reason is blinded by the lusts of the flesh; [[5:12|Having damnation|habentes damnationem]], that is, the cause of eternal damnation, namely mortal sin, [[5:12|because|quia]] [[5:12|they have made void|irritam fecerunt]], that is, have broken, [[5:12|their first faith|primam fidem]], that is, their promise of continence. For to those who have promised chastity, not only to marry but even to will to marry is damnable. [[5:13|And withal|Simul autem]], that is, together with the sins already mentioned, [[5:13|being idle they learn to go about from house to house|et otiosæ existentes discunt circuire domos aliorum]], wandering here and there; [[5:13|not only idle|non solum otiosæ]], since idleness is not long alone but gives birth to other vices, [[5:13|but tattlers also and busy bodies|sed et verbosæ et curiosæ]]: for talkativeness and curiosity are born of idleness[[Ecclus 33:29||]]; [[5:13|speaking things which they ought not|loquentes quæ non oportet]], that is, things unlawful and harmful. He says less, and means more.

paras.t: Volo ergo per modum consulentis, juniores viduas quæ castitatem non promiserunt, nubere, filios procreare, matresfamilias esse, id est domum propriam regere, nullam occasionem dare adversario, id est infideli seu impio, maledicti gratia, id est ad maledicendum seu detrahendum: cui gratum et jucundum est habere aliquid contra fideles, ut possit obloqui eis. Idcirco autem hæc consulo: Jam enim quædam viduæ adolescentiores, post voti emissionem conversæ sunt retro Satanam, id est, a proposito castitatis ceciderunt, rursus nubentes, et dæmonis pravitatem sequentes.
paras.en: [[5:14|I will, therefore|Volo ergo]], by way of counsel, [[5:14|that the younger|juniores]] widows who have not promised chastity [[5:14|should marry, bear children, be mistresses of families|nubere, filios procreare, matresfamilias esse]], that is, govern their own house, [[5:14|give no occasion to the adversary|nullam occasionem dare adversario]], that is, to the unbeliever or the wicked man, [[5:14|to speak evil|maledicti gratia]], that is, for reviling or detraction: for it is pleasing and delightful to him to have something against the faithful, so that he may speak against them. And I counsel this for this reason: [[5:15|For some|Jam enim quædam]] younger widows, after making their vow, [[5:15|are already turned aside after Satan|conversæ sunt retro Satanam]], that is, have fallen from their purpose of chastity, marrying again and following the depravity of the devil.

paras.t: Si quis fidelis habet viduas adolescentes in domo sua, subministret illis necessaria vitæ, et non gravetur Ecclesia Dei eas alendo; ut his quæ vere viduæ sunt et annosæ, de quibus jam dictum est, sufficiat quod habet Ecclesia, scilicet, ut valeat eas sustentare.
paras.en: [[5:16|If any of the faithful have widows|Si quis fidelis habet viduas]] who are young in his house, [[5:16|let him minister to them|subministret illis]] the necessaries of life, [[5:16|and let not the church be charged|et non gravetur Ecclesia]] of God with feeding them; so that for [[5:16|them that are widows indeed|ut his quæ vere viduæ sunt]] and are aged, of whom we have already spoken, [[5:16|there may be sufficient|sufficiat]] what the Church has, that is, that she may be able to support them.

paras.t: Insuper agit Apostolus de presbyterorum honore. Qui bene præsunt presbyteri, id est, qui gregem suum digne custodiunt, duplici honore digni habeantur, id est, præ ceteris copiosius honorentur. Potest autem per duplicem honorem intelligi obedientia et sustentatio: nam subditi presbyteris obedire et stipendia vitæ præbere tenentur. In patria quoque duplici honore digni habentur, videlicet aureæ atque aureolæ. Maxime qui laborant in verbo et doctrina, id est, illi presbyteri potissimum digni sunt duplici honore, qui instant verbo exhortationis quantum ad scientes, et doctrinæ, id est instructionis ignorantium. Quod autem a subditis sint alendi, probat Apostolus auctoritate Scripturæ. Dicit enim Scriptura: Non infrenabis os bovi trituranti, id est, prædicatori non subtrahes necessaria vitæ; et, Dignus est operarius mercede sua. Hoc est quoque superius dictum atque expositum: Non alligabis os bovi triturandi.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle treats of the honour of priests. [[5:17|Let the priests that rule well|Qui bene præsunt presbyteri]], that is, who guard their flock worthily, [[5:17|be esteemed worthy of double honour|duplici honore digni habeantur]], that is, be honoured more abundantly than the rest. By the double honour may be understood obedience and maintenance: for subjects are bound to obey priests and to provide them with the means of living. In the fatherland too [that is, in heaven] they are held worthy of a double honour, namely of the golden crown and of the aureole [the *aurea* is the essential reward of the blessed; the aureole, a special reward added to it for martyrs, virgins and doctors]. [[5:17|especially they who labour in the word and doctrine|Maxime qui laborant in verbo et doctrina]], that is, those priests are most of all worthy of double honour who are diligent in the word of exhortation as regards those who know, and in doctrine, that is, in the instruction of the ignorant. And that they are to be fed by their subjects, the Apostle proves by the authority of Scripture. [[5:18|For the scripture saith|Dicit enim Scriptura]]: [[5:18|Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn|Non infrenabis os bovi trituranti]] [Denis has *infrenabis*, thou shalt not bridle, where the Vulgate has *alligabis*, thou shalt not bind], that is, thou shalt not withdraw from the preacher the necessaries of life; and, [[5:18|The labourer is worthy of his reward|Dignus est operarius mercede sua]]. This too was said and expounded above: [[1 Cor 9:9|Thou shalt not muzzle the mouth of the ox that treadeth out the corn|Non alligabis os bovi triturandi]] [that is, at 1 Cor 9:9, in Denis's commentary on that epistle; the margin gives no reference].

paras.t: Adversus presbyterum noli accusationem recipere, nisi sub duobus aut tribus testibus. Ide digni. Presbyteri enim, quum habeant alios corripere, facile adversarios acquirunt. Veritas enim parit odium. Et ut Salomon profitetur, non amat pestilens eum qui se corripit. Ideo non est accusatio contra presbyterum admittenda, nisi sub duobus testibus ut minimum, vel tribus; et etiam propter dignitatem sui gradus seu ordinis, quum sit Christi vicarius. Peccantes autem testimonio testium convictos, vel aperte excedentes, coram omnibus argue: publica namque peccata, publice arguenda sunt; ut et ceteri superiores ac inferiores, timorem habeant, id est, argui et peccare formident. Si vero peccatum sit occultum, primo occulte arguendus est reus, juxta illud: Si peccaverit in te frater tuus, corripe eum inter te et ipsum solum.
paras.en: [[5:19|Against a priest receive not an accusation|Adversus presbyterum noli accusationem recipere]], [[5:19|but under two or three witnesses|nisi sub duobus aut tribus testibus]]. [the Latin here reads *Ide digni*, which seems corrupt; perhaps *Ideo digni*, “therefore worthy”] For priests, since they have to reprove others, easily gain adversaries. For truth begets hatred [a proverb, from Terence]. And as Solomon declares, [[Prov 15:12|A corrupt man loveth not one that reproveth him|non amat pestilens eum qui se corripit]]. Therefore an accusation is not to be admitted against a priest except under two witnesses at the least, or three; and also on account of the dignity of his degree or order, since he is the vicar of Christ. [[5:20|Them that sin|Peccantes]], convicted by the testimony of witnesses, or openly transgressing, [[5:20|reprove before all|coram omnibus argue]]: for public sins are to be publicly reproved; [[5:20|that the rest also|ut et ceteri]], superiors and inferiors, [[5:20|may have fear|timorem habeant]], that is, may dread to be reproved and to sin. But if the sin is hidden, the guilty man is first to be reproved in secret, according to that saying: [[Matt 18:15|if thy brother shall offend against thee|Si peccaverit in te frater tuus]], [[Matt 18:15|rebuke him between thee and him alone|corripe eum inter te et ipsum solum]].

paras.t: Testor, id est, sub testimonio dico, teque adjuro, coram Deo Patre, et Christo Jesu Filio ejus, et electis, id est sanctis, angelis, ut hæc dicta atque dicenda custodias, non solum memoriter, sed etiam efficienter; sine præjudicio, id est prædiscussione seu præcedenti discretionis judicio, nihil notabile faciens in aliam partem declinando, id est a via justitiæ recedendo ad partem contrariam. Unde in Ecclesiastico legimus: Fili, sine consilio nihil facias, et post factum non pœnitebis. Job quoque: Causam, inquit, quam ignorabam, diligentissime investigabam. Manus cito nemini imposueris, aliquem facile ordinando, sed prius examina eum: neque communicaveris per consensum peccatis alienis.
paras.en: [[5:21|I charge thee|Testor]], that is, I say it under witness and adjure thee, [[5:21|before God|coram Deo]] the Father, [[5:21|and Christ Jesus|et Christo Jesu]] his Son, [[5:21|and the elect|et electis]], that is, holy, [[5:21|angels|angelis]], [[5:21|that thou observe these things|ut hæc dicta atque dicenda custodias]], both those said and those still to be said, not only by memory but also in deed; [[5:21|without prejudice|sine præjudicio]], that is, without prior discussion, or a preceding judgment of discernment [*præjudicium* here is a judgment formed beforehand, after due examination, not prejudice in the modern sense], [[5:21|doing nothing|nihil notabile faciens]] notable [[5:21|by declining to either side|in aliam partem declinando]] [the margin gives the reading *alteram*, as in the Vulgate, for *aliam*], that is, by departing from the way of justice to the contrary side. Hence we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 32:24|My son, do thou nothing without counsel, and thou shalt not repent when thou hast done|Fili, sine consilio nihil facias, et post factum non pœnitebis]]. Job too: [[Job 29:16|the cause|Causam]], he says, [[Job 29:16|which I knew not, I searched out most diligently|quam ignorabam, diligentissime investigabam]]. [[5:22|Impose not hands lightly upon any man|Manus cito nemini imposueris]], by ordaining anyone readily, but first examine him: [[5:22|neither be partaker|neque communicaveris]] by consent [[5:22|of other men's sins|peccatis alienis]].

paras.t: Te ipsum castum custodi, continenter vivendo: quod maxime decet prælatum Ecclesiæ. Noli adhuc aquam bibere, sicut diu fecisti; sed vino modico utere propter stomachum tuum vini calore indigentem (in quo stomacho est sedes ægritudinis, et principium digestionis), et frequentes tuas infirmitates, quæ per aquæ potationem augentur.
paras.en: [[5:22|Keep thyself chaste|Te ipsum castum custodi]], by living continently: which most befits a prelate of the Church. [[5:23|Do not still drink water|Noli adhuc aquam bibere]], as thou hast long done; [[5:23|but use a little wine for thy stomach's sake|sed vino modico utere propter stomachum tuum]], which needs the warmth of wine (in which stomach is the seat of sickness, and the beginning of digestion), [[5:23|and thy frequent infirmities|et frequentes tuas infirmitates]], which are increased by drinking water.

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit Apostolus in quibus necessarium sit præjudicium, seu prævium rationis examen: Quorundam hominum peccata manifesta sunt, id est evidenter mala, quia non possunt bono animo fieri, sicut sunt stupra, furta, blasphemiæ, præcedentia ad judicium, id est nota antequam veniant ad rationis examinationem ac dijudicationem; vel, Præcedentia ad judicium divinum generale seu particulare, quorum utrumque fit post vitam præsentem. Talia ergo non oportet examinari, nec in talibus præjudicium exigitur, sed subito dijudicari possunt. Unde judicium quod ea sequitur, non est temerarium. Quorumdam autem peccata et subsequuntur, id est, peccata aliquorum occulta seu quadam apparenti justitia fucata sunt, ita ut non appareant mala nisi post discussionem: ideo in eis præjudicium est necessarium ut examinentur. Unde nec ea judicare debemus, sed prælatorum et judicum est ea discutere. Vel, Subsequuntur divinum judicium, quia non deducentur in publicum, nisi in die judicii, quando illuminabuntur abscondita tenebrarum. Similiter et facta bona manifesta sunt, id est, aliqua opera bona sunt aperte bona, saltem quantum ad genus operis, quamvis non ad intentionem agentis. Talia ergo examinatione non indigent. Et quæ aliter se habent, id est, bona de quibus mox certum non est an sint veraciter bona, abscondi non possunt, id est, suo tempore clare patebunt, quando a recta ratione examinantur, vel a Deo judicantur. Propter quod in Evangelio Veritas loquitur: Nihil opertum, quod non reveletur; neque occultum, quod non manifestetur.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows in which cases a prior judgment, that is, a previous examination by reason, is necessary: [[5:24|Some men's sins are manifest|Quorundam hominum peccata manifesta sunt]], that is, evidently evil, because they cannot be done with a good intention, such as fornications, thefts, blasphemies, [[5:24|going before to judgment|præcedentia ad judicium]], that is, known before they come to the examination and judgment of reason; or, going before to the divine judgment, general or particular, both of which take place after the present life. Such sins, then, need not be examined, nor is a prior judgment required in such cases, but they can be judged at once. Hence the judgment that follows on them is not rash. [[5:24|and some men|Quorumdam autem]] their sins [[5:24|they follow after|et subsequuntur]], that is, the sins of some are hidden, or coloured with a certain appearance of justice, so that they do not appear evil except after inquiry: therefore in their case a prior judgment is necessary, that they may be examined. Hence we ought not to judge them, but it belongs to prelates and judges to inquire into them. Or: they follow after the divine judgment, because they will not be brought out into public except on the day of judgment, when the Lord [[1 Cor 4:5|will bring to light the hidden things of darkness|illuminabuntur abscondita tenebrarum]] [Denis puts it in the passive: when the hidden things of darkness shall be brought to light]. [[5:25|In like manner also good deeds are manifest|Similiter et facta bona manifesta sunt]], that is, some works are openly good, at least as regards the kind of work, though not as regards the intention of the doer. Such, then, need no examination. [[5:25|and they that are otherwise|Et quæ aliter se habent]], that is, good works of which it is not at once certain whether they are truly good, [[5:25|cannot be hid|abscondi non possunt]], that is, they will be plainly evident in their time, when they are examined by right reason, or judged by God. Wherefore the Truth says in the Gospel: [[Luke 12:2|there is nothing covered that shall not be revealed|Nihil opertum, quod non reveletur]]; nor [[Luke 8:17|any thing secret that shall not be made manifest|neque occultum, quod non manifestetur]].

6.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI SEXTI : QUICUMQUE SUNT SUB JUGO SERVI.
6.title_en: Exposition of the sixth chapter: Whosoever are servants under the yoke.

paras.t: Descendit demum Apostolus ad instructionem particularium personarum. Quicumque sunt sub jugo servi, id est, qualescumque sint servi, videlicet sapientes, fideles, vel alia gratia adornati: tamen quum sint subditi imperio dominorum suorum, dominos suos, tam bonos, quam dyscolos seu infideles, omni honore duliæ, qui carnalibus dominis impendi solet ac debet, dignos arbitrentur: non in quantum infideles et impii, quum scriptum sit de viro justo: Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus. Sciendum, quod quidam docebant libertatem omnibus Christianis esse communem, intendentes servitutem reprobare, eo quod dicat Salvator: Si Filius vos liberaverit, vere liberi eritis; et alibi, Ergo liberi sunt filii. Sed hæc de spirituali libertate, non de carnali, intelligenda sunt. Ideo contra hos fatur Apostolus. Ideo autem servi hoc faciant, ne nomen Domini et doctrina, id est, ne Christus et ejus prædicatio, blasphemetur ab impiis, tanquam sit contra leges, et dominis auferat debitam servitutem.
paras.en: At length the Apostle comes down to the instruction of particular persons. [[6:1|Whosoever are servants under the yoke|Quicumque sunt sub jugo servi]], that is, whatever kind of servants they be, wise, faithful, or adorned with some other grace, yet since they are subject to the rule of their masters, [[6:1|let them count their masters|dominos suos]], the good as well as the froward or unbelieving[[1 Pet 2:18||]], [[6:1|worthy of all honour|omni honore]] of dulia [that is, the honour of service paid to creatures, as distinct from latria, the worship due to God alone], which is wont to be and ought to be paid to masters according to the flesh: not inasmuch as they are unbelieving and wicked, since it is written of the just man: [[Ps 14:4|In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing|Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus]]. Be it known that some taught that freedom is common to all Christians, meaning to condemn servitude, because the Saviour says: [[John 8:36|If therefore the son shall make you free, you shall be free indeed|Si Filius vos liberaverit, vere liberi eritis]]; and elsewhere, [[Matt 17:25|Then the children are free|Ergo liberi sunt filii]]. But these words are to be understood of spiritual freedom, not of fleshly. Therefore the Apostle speaks against these men. And servants are to do this [[6:1|lest the name of the Lord and his doctrine|ne nomen Domini et doctrina]], that is, lest Christ and His preaching, [[6:1|be blasphemed|blasphemetur]] by the wicked, as though it were against the laws and took from masters the service due to them.

paras.t: Qui autem fideles habent dominos, id est servi christianis dominis servientes, non contemnant dominos tales, quia fratres sunt, id est ob hoc quia in Christo sunt pares quantum ad spiritualia; sed magis serviant dominis suis cum debita reverentia, quia domini fideles sunt et dilecti Deo, quia beneficii participes sunt, id est, domini eadem beneficia gratiæ a Deo receperunt atque recipiunt, quæ et servi. Hæc doce servos et exhortare eos, ut sic agant.
paras.en: [[6:2|But they that have believing masters|Qui autem fideles habent dominos]], that is, servants who serve Christian masters, [[6:2|let them not despise|non contemnant]] such masters [[6:2|because they are brethren|quia fratres sunt]], that is, on the ground that in Christ they are equals as regards spiritual things; [[6:2|but serve them the rather|sed magis serviant]], their masters, with due reverence, [[6:2|because|quia]] the masters [[6:2|are faithful and beloved|fideles sunt et dilecti]] of God, [[6:2|who are partakers of the benefit|quia beneficii participes sunt]] [Denis reads *quia*, 'because they are partakers'], that is, the masters have received and receive from God the same benefits of grace as the servants too. [[6:2|These things teach|Hæc doce]] the servants, [[6:2|and exhort|et exhortare]] them to act thus.

paras.t: Si quis aliter docet, quam ego jam docui, et non acquiescit sanis, id est veris, sermonibus Domini nostri Jesu Christi, quos loquitur per me, qui etiam proprio ore dixit, Reddite quæ sunt Cæsaris, Cæsari; et ei, quæ secundum pietatem est, doctrinæ evangelicæ, quæ ad pietatem inducit, et lites odiumque exstirpat.
paras.en: [[6:3|If any man teach otherwise|Si quis aliter docet]] than I have now taught, [[6:3|and consent not to the sound|et non acquiescit sanis]], that is, true, [[6:3|words of our Lord Jesus Christ|sermonibus Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], which He speaks through me, who also said with His own mouth, [[Matt 22:21|Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar's|Reddite quæ sunt Cæsaris, Cæsari]]; [[6:3|and to that doctrine which is according to godliness|et ei, quæ secundum pietatem est, doctrinæ]], the doctrine of the Gospel, which leads to godliness and roots out quarrels and hatred.

paras.t: Talis superbus est, nihil sciens scientia salutari et formata, de qua dicitur a Sapiente: Dedit illi scientiam Sanctorum. Unde et Salomon: Ubi, inquit, humilitas, ibi sapientia; et rursus, Superbus et arrogans vocatur indoctus. Sed languens, id est cum infirmitate sui intellectus inaniter occupatus, circa quæstiones et pugnas, id est disputationes litigiosas, verborum: ex quibus oriuntur invidiæ unius in alium, contentiones, blasphemiæ adversariorum fidei contra Deum, dum audiunt aliqua rationi naturali contraria, suspiciones malæ, conflictationes hominum mente corruptorum, id est infectam voluntatem habentium, aversorum a summo et incommutabili bono: de quibus Propheta inquit, Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt; et qui veritate privati sunt, id est spiritualiter excæcati. Hominum, inquam, existimantium quæstum esse pietatem, id est opus pietatis, videlicet prædicationem, ordinandum esse ad lucrum temporale. Nam ideo prædicant, ut temporale commodum consequantur, quemadmodum apud Michæam prophetam de quibusdam inducitur: Sacerdotes ejus in mercede docebant, et prophetæ ejus in pecunia divinabant.
paras.en: Such a one [[6:4|is proud, knowing nothing|superbus est, nihil sciens]] with the knowledge that saves and is formed [that is, quickened by charity], of which the Wise Man says: [[Wis 10:10|gave him the knowledge of the holy things|Dedit illi scientiam Sanctorum]]. Hence Solomon too: Where, he says, [[Prov 11:2|humility is, there also is wisdom|humilitas, ibi sapientia]]; and again, [[Prov 21:24|The proud and the arrogant is called ignorant|Superbus et arrogans vocatur indoctus]]. [[6:4|But sick|Sed languens]], that is, busied to no purpose with the weakness of his understanding, [[6:4|about questions and strifes|circa quæstiones et pugnas]], that is, quarrelsome disputations, [[6:4|of words|verborum]]: [[6:4|from which arise envies|ex quibus oriuntur invidiæ]] of one against another, [[6:4|contentions, blasphemies|contentiones, blasphemiæ]] of the adversaries of the faith against God, when they hear things contrary to natural reason, [[6:4|evil suspicions|suspiciones malæ]], [[6:5|Conflicts of men corrupted in mind|conflictationes hominum mente corruptorum]], that is, of men whose will is infected, turned away from the highest and unchangeable good: of whom the Prophet says, [[Osee 10:2|Their heart is divided: now they shall perish|Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt]]; [[6:5|and who are destitute of the truth|et qui veritate privati sunt]], that is, spiritually blinded. Of men, I say, [[6:5|supposing gain to be godliness|existimantium quæstum esse pietatem]], that is, that the work of godliness, namely preaching, is to be directed to temporal profit. For they preach in order to obtain temporal advantage, as is said of some in the prophet Micheas: [[Mich 3:11|her priests have taught for hire, and her prophets divined for money|Sacerdotes ejus in mercede docebant, et prophetæ ejus in pecunia divinabant]].

paras.t: Est autem quæstus magnus, pietas cum sufficientia: id est, quamvis pietas non sit quæstus carnalis ac temporalis, ut illi existimant; est tamen magnus quæstus, videlicet fructuosus, spiritualis atque æternus, quia æternam vitam meretur. Estque acquisitio omnium spiritualium divitiarum pietas ista, id est cultus Dei cum sufficientia victus ac vestium, sicut jam dictum est, Pietas ad omnia utilis est, promissionem habens vitæ quæ nunc est, et futuræ: cum qua sufficientia debemus esse contenti.
paras.en: [[6:6|But godliness with contentment is great gain.|Est autem quæstus magnus, pietas cum sufficientia]] [Latin *sufficientia*, 'sufficiency', which the Douay-Rheims renders 'contentment']: that is, although godliness is not a fleshly and temporal gain, as those men suppose, it is yet a great gain, namely a fruitful, spiritual and eternal one, because it merits eternal life. And this godliness, that is, the worship of God with a sufficiency of food and clothing, is the acquiring of all spiritual riches, as has been said already, [[1 Tim 4:8|godliness is profitable to all things, having promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come|Pietas ad omnia utilis est, promissionem habens vitæ quæ nunc est, et futuræ]]: with which sufficiency we ought to be content.

paras.t: Nihil enim temporalium divitiarum intulimus in hunc mundum, nascendo: sicut Job ait, Nudus egressus sum de utero matris meæ; haud, id est non, dubium est, sed certum, quia nec auferre mundo quid talium rerum possumus moriendo: sicut ait Psalmista, Homo quum interierit, non sumet omnia; et Job: Dives quum dormierit, nihil secum auferet; apprehendet eum quasi aqua inopia.
paras.en: [[6:7|For we brought nothing|Nihil enim]] of temporal riches [[6:7|into this world|intulimus in hunc mundum]] in being born: as Job says, [[Job 1:21|Naked came I out of my mother's womb|Nudus egressus sum de utero matris meæ]]; [[6:7|certainly|haud]] (that is, it is not doubtful, but certain) [[6:7|we can carry nothing out|nec auferre]] of the world, of such things, in dying: as the Psalmist says, Man, [[Ps 48:18|when he shall die he shall take nothing away|quum interierit, non sumet omnia]] [the margin gives only Ps. xlviii]; and Job: [[Job 27:19|The rich man when he shall sleep shall take away nothing with him|Dives quum dormierit, nihil secum auferet]]; [[Job 27:20|Poverty like water shall take hold on him|apprehendet eum quasi aqua inopia]] [the margin gives Job xxvii, 18, 19, 20].

paras.t: Habentes autem alimenta et indumenta quibus tegamur, id est victualium et vestimentorum competentiam, his contenti simus, quantum ad appetitum temporalium rerum. Qui enim ultra procedit, inordinate se habet, et superflue agit: quoniam corporalia ad spiritualia ordinantur sicut media ad finem, ideo non sunt appetenda nisi ad necessitatem, videlicet in tantum quantum conferunt vel requiruntur ad spiritualem mentis profectum, quem superfluitas temporalium rerum non provehit, sed impedit. Ideo Sapiens orabat: Divitias ne dederis mihi, tribue tantum victui meo necessaria.
paras.en: [[6:8|But having food|Habentes autem alimenta]] and clothing [[6:8|wherewith to be covered|quibus tegamur]], that is, a sufficiency of victuals and garments, [[6:8|with these we are content|his contenti simus]] [Latin *simus*, 'let us be content'], as regards the desire of temporal things. For he who goes beyond this behaves inordinately and acts superfluously: since bodily things are ordered to spiritual ones as means to an end, they are therefore not to be desired except for necessity, namely so far as they help or are required for the spiritual progress of the mind, which an excess of temporal things does not further, but hinders. Therefore the Wise Man prayed: Give me not [[Prov 30:8|riches|Divitias ne dederis mihi]]; [[Prov 30:8|give me only the necessaries of life|tribue tantum victui meo necessaria]].

paras.t: Nam qui volunt, id est, volendo satisagunt, divites fieri, incidunt in tentationem, id est in diabolicam impugnationem, et in laqueum diaboli, id est in peccati consensum, quo anima a diabolo capitur quasi in laqueo. Tales enim quum sint avari, aliorum bona desiderant, alienis prosperitatibus invident, et per vitiosa media conantur temporalia congregare, mentiendo, fallendo, etc. Ideo enim in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: Avaro nihil est scelestius; et nihil est iniquius quam amare pecuniam. Christus quoque in Evangelio: Possibilius, inquit, est camelum per foramen acus transire, quam divitem (id est divitiarum amatorem) intrare in regnum cœlorum. Incidunt quoque et in desideria multa inordinata: de quibus Joannes, Omne, inquit, quod est in mundo, aut est concupiscentia oculorum, aut concupiscentia carnis, aut superbia vitæ; et inutilia et nociva. Hæc enim desideria sunt inutilia, quia non prosunt ad adipiscendam veram salutem; et nociva, quoniam gratiam Dei exstinguunt (id est, […]) […]mines avaros in interitum, id est gratiæ amissionem, quæ est mors animæ, et perdilitiæ gloriæ sempiternæ, quæ est mors secunda ac infernalis. Hæc enim mala inferunt desideria ista.
paras.en: [[6:9|For they that will|Nam qui volunt]], that is, who busy themselves in willing, [[6:9|become rich|divites fieri]], [[6:9|fall into temptation|incidunt in tentationem]], that is, into the assault of the devil, [[6:9|and into the snare of the devil|et in laqueum diaboli]], that is, into consent to sin, by which the soul is caught by the devil as in a snare. For such men, being covetous, desire the goods of others, envy the prosperity of others, and try to gather temporal things by wicked means, by lying, by deceiving, etc. For this reason it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:9|nothing is more wicked than the covetous man|Avaro nihil est scelestius]]; and [[Ecclus 10:10|There is not a more wicked thing than to love money|nihil est iniquius quam amare pecuniam]]. Christ too in the Gospel: It is more possible, He says, [[Matt 19:24|for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle|camelum per foramen acus transire]], [[Matt 19:24|than for a rich man|quam divitem]] (that is, a lover of riches) [[Matt 19:24|to enter into the kingdom of heaven|intrare in regnum cœlorum]] [there is no margin reference here; Denis has *possibilius*, 'more possible', for the Gospel's *facilius*, 'easier']. They fall also [[6:9|into many|in desideria multa]] disordered desires: of which John says, All [[1 John 2:16|that is in the world|quod est in mundo]] is either [[1 John 2:16|the concupiscence of the eyes|concupiscentia oculorum]], or [[1 John 2:16|the concupiscence of the flesh|concupiscentia carnis]], or [[1 John 2:16|the pride of life|superbia vitæ]]; [[6:9|unprofitable and hurtful|et inutilia et nociva]]. For these desires are unprofitable, because they are of no avail for gaining true salvation; and hurtful, because they extinguish the grace of God (that is, […]) […] covetous men [[6:9|into destruction|in interitum]], that is, the loss of grace, which is the death of the soul, and perdition of everlasting glory [the printed word is garbled here, *perdilitiæ*; the sense is the loss of glory], which is the second and infernal death. For these are the evils that these desires bring on.

paras.t: Radix enim omnium malorum cupiditas est, cupiditas plus habendi quam expedit. Nec obstat quod superbia dicitur omnis peccati initium, vel etiam amor privatus, cui maxime convenit esse omnium peccatorum originem. Nam, sicut nullum est peccati quod non oriatur (ut plurimum) ex superbia, sic nullum est genus peccati quod non interdum nascatur ex cupiditate, et e contrario. Sunt enim qui non amarent superflua, nisi per possessionem illorum putarent se excellentiores esse futuros; et […]
paras.en: [[6:10|For the desire of money is the root of all evils|Radix enim omnium malorum cupiditas est]], the desire of having more than is expedient. Nor does it stand in the way that pride is called [[Ecclus 10:15|the beginning of all sin|omnis peccati initium]] [the margin gives Eccli. xx; the words are Ecclus 10:15], or private love too [that is, a man's disordered love of his own good], to which above all it belongs to be the origin of all sins. For as there is no sin that does not (for the most part) spring from pride, so there is no kind of sin that is not sometimes born of covetousness, and the other way about. For there are those who would not love superfluous things unless they thought that by possessing them they would be more excellent; and […]

paras.t: […] omne tempus comprehendit. Nam et in patria erit post diem judicii, tempus discretum, ut Thomas et alii multi testantur. Ostendet hominibus bonis et malis in die judicii, sed solis electis in die æternitatis, beatus et solus potens, id est Deus Trinitas substantialiter felix: in quo est omnium bonorum, pulchrorum ac desiderabilium infinita plenitudo; qui solus essentialiter potens est, et ipsa sua potentia. De quo in Job conscriptum est: Deus potentes non abjicit, quum et ipse sit potens. Rex regum et Dominus dominantium. Omnia namque quantumcumque potentia atque sublimia, comparantur ad Deum sicut instrumenta ad artificem, sicut media ad finem, et sicut subjecti ad principem. Unde ait Psalmista: Quoniam Deus magnus Dominus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos.
paras.en: […] takes in all time. For in the fatherland too, after the day of judgement, there will be a distinct time, as Thomas and many others testify. He [[6:15|shall shew|ostendet]], to men good and wicked on the day of judgement, but to the elect alone on the day of eternity, [[6:15|who is the Blessed and only Mighty|beatus et solus potens]], that is, God the Trinity, blessed in His substance: in whom is the infinite fulness of all good, beautiful and desirable things; who alone is mighty in His essence, and is His own might. Of whom it is written in Job: [[Job 36:5|God doth not cast away the mighty, whereas he himself also is mighty|Deus potentes non abjicit, quum et ipse sit potens]]. [[6:15|the King of kings and Lord of lords|Rex regum et Dominus dominantium]][[Apoc 19:16||]]. For all things, however mighty and lofty, are compared to God as instruments to the craftsman, as means to the end, and as subjects to the prince. Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 94:3|For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods|Quoniam Deus magnus Dominus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos]] [the margin gives Ps. xcv; the words are Ps 94:3].

paras.t: Qui solus per naturam habet immortalitatem, id est omnimodam et superplenissimam invariabilitatem, sicut per Malachiam loquitur: Ego Dominus, et non mutor. Omne autem creatum aliquo modo mutabile est, et in omni ente mutabili invenitur quædam mortalitas, secundum Augustinum, videlicet alicujus desinentia, et recens dispositio. Et lucem habitat inaccessibilem: id est, nullo loco vel termino clauditur, nec in aliqua creatura per circumscriptionem moratur, sed habitat in se ipso per quietissimam subsistentiam; qui est lux supersubstantialis, vera et infinita: quæ inaccessibilis dicitur, quia a nullo intellectu creato comprehendi potest. Unde et dicitur tenebras ponere latibulum suum. Potest tamen homo ad eam accedere in via per fidem et gratiam, et in patria per claram visionem. Propter quod ait Psalmista: Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini. Et ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus: Accedamus cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ ejus. Quem nullus hominum vidit, exsistens homo purus, et sensitivarum virium operationibus ablatus; […] potest in hac vita visione clara per speciem, qua cognoscitur de re quid est. Potest tamen videri per fidem et speciem creatam, qua cognoscitur quia est. Propter quod scriptum est in Job: Omnes homines vident Deum, unusquisque intuetur procul. Prædictis vero verbis Apostoli consonat et illud Joannis: Deum nemo vidit unquam; et quod Moysi Dominus dicebat, Non videbit me homo, et vivet. His ergo non obviat, quod non solum Christus, sed Moyses quoque et Paulus Deum per speciem in hac vita viderunt, secundum Augustinum. Pro tunc enim non vixerunt vita humana et sensitiva. Cui Deo trino ac simplici est honor latriæ, et imperium sempiternum: juxta illud Danielis, Potestas ejus potestas sempiterna, et regnum ejus in generationem et generationem. Amen.
paras.en: [[6:16|Who only|Qui solus]] by nature [[6:16|hath immortality|habet immortalitatem]], that is, an unchangeableness that is complete in every way and more than full, as He says by Malachias: [[Mal 3:6|I am the Lord, and I change not|Ego Dominus, et non mutor]]. But every created thing is in some way changeable, and in every changeable being there is found a certain mortality, according to Augustine, namely the ceasing of something and a fresh disposition. [[6:16|and inhabiteth light inaccessible|Et lucem habitat inaccessibilem]]: that is, He is shut in by no place or bound, nor does He dwell in any creature by circumscription [that is, by being contained within limits, as a body is in a place], but dwells in Himself by a most tranquil subsistence; He who is light supersubstantial, true and infinite[[1 John 1:5||]]: which is called inaccessible because it cannot be comprehended by any created intellect. Hence too it is said that He [[Ps 17:12|made darkness his cover|tenebras ponere latibulum suum]] [the margin gives Ps. xcvi, 12; the words are Ps 17:12]. Yet man can draw near to it on the way [that is, in this life] by faith and grace, and in the fatherland by clear vision. For this reason the Psalmist says: [[Ps 33:6|Come ye to him and be enlightened|Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini]]. And the Apostle says to the Hebrews: Let us go [[Heb 4:16|with confidence to the throne of grace|cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ]] of Him. [[6:16|whom no man hath seen|Quem nullus hominum vidit]], being a mere man, and withdrawn from the operations of the powers of sense; […] can in this life by clear vision through the essence [Latin *species*: the vision of God as He is in Himself], by which it is known of a thing what it is. Yet He can be seen through faith and a created likeness [*species creata*], by which it is known that He is.
