For this reason it is written in Job: [[Job 36:25|All men see him, every one beholdeth afar off|Omnes homines vident Deum, unusquisque intuetur procul]] [the margin gives Job xxxvi, 24; Denis has *Deum*, 'God', for *eum*, 'him']. With the foregoing words of the Apostle that saying of John agrees: [[John 1:18|No man hath seen God at any time|Deum nemo vidit unquam]]; and what the Lord said to Moses, [[Ex 33:20|man shall not see me, and live|Non videbit me homo, et vivet]]. With these, then, it does not conflict that not only Christ, but Moses too and Paul saw God through His essence in this life, according to Augustine. For at that time they were not living the human life of the senses. [[6:16|to whom|Cui]], God three and simple, [[6:16|be honour|est honor]] of latria [that is, the worship due to God alone], [[6:16|and empire everlasting|et imperium sempiternum]]: according to that of Daniel, [[Dan 4:31|his power is an everlasting power, and his kingdom is to all generations|Potestas ejus potestas sempiterna, et regnum ejus in generationem et generationem]] [the margin gives Dan. vii, 14; Denis's words are those of Dan 4:31]. [[6:16|Amen|Amen]].

paras.t: Superius dixit Apostolus quid contingat volentibus ditari; nunc docet quid oporteat divites facere. Divitibus hujus sæculi, id est temporales et sæculares divitias habentibus, præcipe, quod et Scriptura divina præcipit: non sublime sapere, id est de divitiis non extolli, nec alios aspernari, neque sperare in incerto divitiarum, id est in istis amissibilibus divitiis quæ sunt bona fortunæ. Propter quod ait Psalmista: Divitiæ si affluant, nolite cor apponere. Et Job: Si putavi, inquit, aurum robur meum, et obryzo dixi, Fiducia mea. Quam autem difficile et rarum sit hoc, patet per illud Ecclesiastici: Beatus dives qui inventus est sine macula, qui post aurum non abiit, nec speravit in pecuniæ thesauris. Quis est hic? et laudabimus eum: fecit enim mirabilia in vita sua. Hinc et Christus in Evangelio asserit: Quam difficile qui habent pecunias, intrabunt in regnum cælorum! Sed hoc […] vivo, omnis vitæ fontano principio, de quo ait Propheta: Domine virtutum, beatus homo qui sperat in te: qui præstat nobis omnia corporalia ac spiritualia quæ habemus, abunde, id est copiose, juxta illud Jacobi: Qui dat omnibus affluenter, et non improperat, […] id est ad alium dum temporalibus […] ut sic utantur præsentibus, quatenus bonis futuris nobis promissis, quæ oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit, tandem fruamur.
paras.en: Above, the Apostle said what befalls those who wish to grow rich; now he teaches what the rich must do. [[6:17|the rich of this world|Divitibus hujus sæculi]], that is, those who have temporal and worldly riches, [[6:17|Charge|præcipe]] what divine Scripture too commands: [[6:17|not to be highminded|non sublime sapere]], that is, not to be puffed up over riches, nor to despise others, [[6:17|nor to trust in the uncertainty of riches|neque sperare in incerto divitiarum]], that is, in these riches that can be lost, which are goods of fortune. For this reason the Psalmist says: [[Ps 61:11|if riches abound, set not your heart upon them|Divitiæ si affluant, nolite cor apponere]]. And Job: [[Job 31:24|If I have thought|Si putavi]], he says, [[Job 31:24|gold my strength, and have said to fine gold: My confidence|aurum robur meum, et obryzo dixi, Fiducia mea]]. But how hard and rare this is appears from that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 31:8|Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures|Beatus dives qui inventus est sine macula, qui post aurum non abiit, nec speravit in pecuniæ thesauris]]. [[Ecclus 31:9|Who is he, and we will praise him? for he hath done wonderful things in his life.|Quis est hic? et laudabimus eum: fecit enim mirabilia in vita sua]] Hence Christ too declares in the Gospel: [[Mark 10:23|How hardly shall they that have riches|Quam difficile qui habent pecunias]] [[Mark 10:23|enter into the kingdom|intrabunt in regnum]] of heaven! [Denis has *cælorum*, 'of heaven', for *Dei*, 'of God'.] But […] [[6:17|living|vivo]] [the transcription reads *Sed hoc vivo*; the lemma is *sed in Deo vivo*, 'but in the living God'], the fountain-head and principle of all life, of whom the Prophet says: [[Ps 83:13|O Lord of hosts, blessed is the man that trusteth in thee|Domine virtutum, beatus homo qui sperat in te]]: [[6:17|who giveth us|qui præstat nobis]] [[6:17|all things|omnia]] bodily and spiritual that we have, [[6:17|abundantly|abunde]], that is, plentifully, according to that saying of James: [[Jas 1:5|who giveth to all men abundantly and upbraideth not|Qui dat omnibus affluenter, et non improperat]], […] that is, to another […] with temporal things […] that they may so use present things that at length we may enjoy the good things to come promised us, which [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard|oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit]].

paras.t: Præcipe insuper divitibus, bene agere, divites fieri in operibus bonis, id est spirituales divitias congregare, videlicet cumulum meritorum, et incrementa gratiæ atque virtutum, prout ait Salvator: Thesaurizate vobis thesauros in cœlo; facile tribuere eleemosynas, quemadmodum Christus hortatur: Omni petenti te tribue; et, Beatius est magis dare quam accipere; communicare, id est communia reputare vel facere bona exteriora; thesaurizare sibi fundamentum bonum, id est stabilem cordis adhæsionem cum Deo, seu opus meritorium, in futurum, id est ad hoc ut digni sint bonis sæculi futuri, ut apprehendant veram vitam, id est, æternam vitam seu beatitudinem quæ non est fallax et labilis, consequantur.
paras.en: Charge the rich, moreover, [[6:18|To do good|bene agere]], [[6:18|to be rich in good work|divites fieri in operibus bonis]], that is, to gather spiritual riches, namely a store of merits and increase of grace and virtues, as the Saviour says: [[Matt 6:20|lay up to yourselves treasures in heaven|Thesaurizate vobis thesauros in cœlo]]; [[6:18|to give easily|facile tribuere]] alms, as Christ exhorts: [[Luke 6:30|Give to every one that asketh thee|Omni petenti te tribue]]; and, [[Acts 20:35|It is a more blessed thing to give, rather than to receive|Beatius est magis dare quam accipere]]; [[6:18|to communicate to others|communicare]], that is, to hold or make outward goods common; [[6:19|To lay up in store for themselves a good foundation|thesaurizare sibi fundamentum bonum]], that is, a steadfast cleaving of the heart to God, or meritorious work, [[6:19|against the time to come|in futurum]], that is, so that they may be worthy of the goods of the world to come, [[6:19|that they may lay hold on the true life|ut apprehendant veram vitam]], that is, may obtain eternal life or beatitude, which is not deceitful and slippery.

paras.t: O Timothee, depositum custodi, id est, episcopale officium tibi divinitus commendatum seu creditum diligenter exerce, et gratiam tibi concessam, creditaque talenta, suo tempore cum usuris repetenda, sollicite conserva, expende, dispensa; devitans profanas vocum novitates, id est nova vocabula Religioni sanctæ contraria, quæ sua obscuritate vel vanitate introducunt errorem. Ponit autem Glossa exemplum de nomine isto, Hypostasis; sed hoc intelligendum est pro certo tempore. Hypostasis namque significat essentiam et personam. Unde hæretici per usum hujus nominis volebant catholicos inducere ad confitendum tres essentias in divinis, sicut et tres Personas. Idcirco non licuit nomine isto uti ante determinationem suæ significationis. Nunc vero, quoniam usu doctorum determinatum est ad significandum personam, licitum est ipso uti: imo doctores ut plurimum ipso utuntur. Hinc Dionysius, et eum sequens Damascenus, affirmant, non esse audendum aliud de supersubstantiali Deitate asserere, præter ea quæ nobis in sacris eloquiis tradita sunt. Et Hieronymus dicit: Ex sola inordinata prolatione verborum incurritur hæresis. Devitans etiam et oppositiones, id est instantias seu contradictiones contra fidem, falsi nominis scientiæ, id est vanæ scientiæ, quæ mendaciter scientia appellatur, ut est omnis scientia quæ se extollit contra scientiam Dei seu fidei veritatem;
paras.en: [[6:20|O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust|O Timothee, depositum custodi]], that is, exercise diligently the episcopal office committed or entrusted to thee by God, and carefully keep, spend and dispense the grace granted thee and the talents entrusted to thee, which will be asked back with interest in their time[[Matt 25:27||]]; [[6:20|avoiding the profane novelties of words|devitans profanas vocum novitates]], that is, new terms contrary to holy Religion, which by their obscurity or vanity bring in error. The Gloss gives as an example the word *hypostasis*; but this is to be understood for a certain time. For *hypostasis* signifies both essence and person. Hence heretics, through the use of this word, wished to lead Catholics to confess three essences in God, as well as three Persons. Therefore it was not lawful to use this word before its meaning was settled. But now, since by the usage of the doctors it has been settled to signify person, it is lawful to use it; indeed the doctors use it for the most part. Hence Dionysius, and Damascene following him, affirm that we must not dare to assert anything of the supersubstantial Godhead beyond what has been handed down to us in the sacred oracles. And Jerome says: By the disordered utterance of words alone heresy is incurred. Avoiding also [[6:20|and oppositions|et oppositiones]], that is, objections or contradictions against the faith, [[6:20|of knowledge falsely so called|falsi nominis scientiæ]], that is, of vain knowledge, which is falsely called knowledge, as is all knowledge that exalts itself against the knowledge of God or the truth of the faith;

paras.t: quam falsam scientiam quidam promittentes, id est se habere et diligere profitentes, circa fidem exciderunt, id est, a fide catholica corruerunt, sequentes naturalem rationem et propriam imaginationem, imo stultitiam potius quam divinam auctoritatem. Gratia tecum: quæ non infunditur nisi ab Omnipotente, qui est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: [[6:21|Which|quam]] false knowledge [[6:21|some promising|quidam promittentes]], that is, professing to have and love it, [[6:21|have erred concerning the faith|circa fidem exciderunt]], that is, have fallen away from the Catholic faith, following natural reason and their own imagination, or rather folly, rather than divine authority. [[6:21|Grace be with thee|Gratia tecum]]: which is poured in by none but the Almighty, who is God above all, exalted and blessed. [[6:21|Amen|Amen]].
